question.prompt: Choose 2 from 4 distinct elements, without regard to order. How many selections are there?

solutions.explanation: There are 12 ways when order matters. When order is disregarded, each combination corresponds to 2 permutations, so \(12/2=6\).
solutions.title: Count ordered selections

solutions.explanation: Label the four elements \(A,B,C,D\). Write each pair with its alphabetically earlier element first, so changing the order cannot repeat a selection. The complete list is \(AB,AC,AD,BC,BD,CD\), giving \(6\) selections.
solutions.title: List each pair once
